hypothesis: Keeping OLMoE attention q/k/v/o and lm_head half-resident (widened to f32 per element, same matmul lanes) halves the dense bytes a cached decode step streams from DRAM, so tokens/s rises with no change to any value.
model: OLMoE-1B-7B-Instruct, Colibri int8-expert container (dense tensors FP16 on disk), 7.2 GB
command: make -C c olmoe; for each arm, alternating B,T,T,B,... after one warm-up pair: SNAP=<model> COLI_TEMP=0 COLI_DENSE_F16=<0|1> PPL=1 ./olmoe 64 8 ref_pr.json (tok_s = the Speed line: 256 teacher-forced decode steps + 24-token prefill); quality: same ref with PPL unset, greedy generate of 128 tokens, token streams compared; the measured binary was built from afeab04d (this change on top of the FUSED3 gate fix in #2039): FUSED3 is off in both arms, so the two trees run identical code on this path

hardware.cpu: 12th Gen Intel Core i7-12700H, 14 cores / 20 threads (6P+8E), AVX2/F16C/FMA
hardware.ram: 16 GB DDR4-3200 (single 16 GB module, as reported by Win32_PhysicalMemory)
hardware.storage: WD PC SN740 512 GB NVMe, NTFS; model files read through the OS page cache (warm after the first pair)
hardware.os: Windows 11 Education 10.0.26200, gcc 16.1.0 (MinGW-W64 ucrt, Brecht Sanders r4), -O3 -march=x86-64-v3 -fopenmp; laptop on mains power

config.fixed: SNAP=OLMoE-1B-7B-Instruct int8 experts, COLI_TEMP=0, PPL=1 teacher-forced 24-token prompt + 256 tokens, cap 64 (every expert cached), bits 8, OMP defaults

quality.method: TF-NLL 1.4863 and greedy 128-token stream identical to the trial arm
